column2: req_desc

Parameter manifest
Each part's parameters are served in declaration order with label, kind, unit, default, limits, group, derived flag, and a step and display precision derived from the default when the source declares none.

Dimension fields by keyboard
A visitor reaches every dimension control by Tab and sets it with the arrow, Page, Ctrl or Meta, and Shift keys, each press committing one clamped value.

Modified marker, units and Reset all
A control whose value differs from its default shows the was marker and an amber frame, the rail header counts modified values, Reset all restores every default in one evaluation, and Units switches the shown lengths between millimetres and inches.

Configuration address
Once the evaluation debounce elapses the address bar carries only non-default values sorted by name, or an empty config at the defaults, without a reload, and loading that address restores the same configuration.

Readouts update in place
After each settled evaluation the volume, bounding box, face count and digest readouts and the viewport attributes change in place and the Evaluation live region announces the result.

One evaluation per burst
Commits within the evaluation debounce send exactly one evaluation, carrying the next sequence number for that page.

Evaluation record
Every evaluation is answered and stored as the published evaluation JSON and can be read back by its id.

Superseded evaluations cancelled
A commit made while an evaluation is in flight aborts its request and cancels it on the server, its record reads cancelled, the Evaluation region announces the supersession and the controls stay editable throughout.

Latest result wins
A response older than the newest applied sequence is dropped without touching the viewport, and no re-evaluation ever changes the camera pose, empties the viewport or moves the selected finding.

Slow evaluation notice
An evaluation still running after the slow-evaluation threshold shows the published notice under the viewport until it ends.

Tine operations and measures
The evaluator accepts the published Tine grammar and reports volume, bounding box and face count exactly as the operation table defines.

Geometry digest
The geometry digest is the SHA-256 of the solid's Tinework canonical JSON, which is stored and served byte for byte, so parameter sets that resolve to the same solid share a digest.

Diagnostics and limits
Invalid geometry, oversize values, too many operations and over-time evaluations fail with the published diagnostic code and text.

Failed value keeps the last good solid
When a committed value fails, the viewport keeps drawing the last good solid and digest, the typed value stays in its control, the diagnostic shows in Findings and is announced, and a corrected value returns to settled.

Opening a shared configuration
Anyone opening a configuration address sees the same values, digest and volume as the sender.

Dropped link values
Unknown names and unusable values in a configuration address are dropped, the rest apply, the address is rewritten without them, and Findings lists the dropped names.

Sign up to save
A signed-out visitor who saves is asked to sign up, the verification link returns them to the same configuration with Save revision open and the sign-up dialog gone, and a return address that is not a single-slash path lands on the home page.

Saved only once stored
A revision is created, shown as saved and listed only after its solid, source and every tape step solid are confirmed in storage.

Saving someone else's part
A signed-in visitor who saves a part they do not own gets a private copy titled with the my configuration suffix and lands on the copy's page with this configuration as r1 and Saved r1. announced.

Phone viewport edge to edge
Below 1024 pixels wide the viewport spans the full window width from its left edge with the rail groups stacked under it, and at 390 by 844 a visitor edits dimensions there by touch.

One open group, closed groups inert
Below 1024 pixels only one rail group is open at a time and every control in a closed group is hidden, unfocusable and absent from the accessibility tree.

Scrub by pointer and touch
Dragging a captured scrub handle changes the value one step per 4 pixels and commits only on release, while Escape or a cancelled pointer restores the starting value and commits nothing.

Pre-flight findings
Running pre-flight against a chosen process returns wall, hole depth and envelope findings with the published texts, computed only from that request's own values and process, or the unsupported line for a laser-cut part with a boss.

Finding order and severity labels
Findings are ordered Blocking then Advisory by shortfall, each labelled with its severity word and icon, and a part with no findings shows one Pass row.

Cost band and confidence
Each report shows cost bands at quantities 1, 10 and 100, a confidence level and the permanent estimate line, computed by the published formula.

Walking findings by keyboard
A visitor chooses a process with arrow keys, runs pre-flight, and selecting a finding by Enter, Space or a click glides the camera to its stored pose.

Finding camera under reduced motion
With reduced motion, selecting a finding or hunk applies the same end pose in one frame.

Stale report
Changing a parameter or process after a report, or during its run, marks it stale, dims its findings and shows the staleness banner without re-running it, and returning to the report's values and process makes it complete again.

Signed-out pre-flight allowance
A signed-out session may run the published number of reports, claimed atomically, the run button shows how many are left, and a run beyond it is refused with 429, Retry-After and the sign-in line.

Compare volumes
Comparing two revisions reports added, removed and unchanged volume from their stored solids on the published voxel grid, or the no-change line when both digests are equal, and only the newest selected pair is ever painted.

Hunks by keyboard
J and K walk the compare hunks in published order from any non-text control, ignored while an input method is composing, each selection moving the camera to the hunk's pose.

New revisions arrive live on compare
A revision saved anywhere appears in both compare menus and is announced on every open page of the part within 2 seconds, keeping the selected hunk and focus.

Review room and invitation
A part owner opens a review room with at least the required number of reviewers, and each reviewer receives one invitation mail with the room link, revision label and head volume.

Comments and anchors
Reviewers and the owner post comments stored normalised up to the published length counted in grapheme segments, anchored to a point or to a view, each storing the camera pose and head revision.

Live comments
A comment appears in Threads only once the server accepts it or its live event arrives, reaches every other open room page within 2 seconds, is announced in Room activity and restores its pose when selected, and a lost, refused or closed-room post shows its published line with no comment added.

Selection holds through live updates
The selected thread, hunk or finding and the focused control stay selected and focused while live comments, revisions or evaluations repaint the page.

Approval rules
A reviewer approves only the room's head revision, the owner cannot approve, each refusal returns its published status and message, and simultaneous duplicate approvals make one record with exactly one 201.

Approval progress live
Each approval updates the progress and state on every open room page within 2 seconds, and reaching the required count marks the room approved.

Approvals follow the head's geometry
A new head with a different digest reopens the room live when the counted approvals drop, one with the same digest carries them over, and one matching earlier approved geometry counts them again, each with its published line.

Immutable revisions
Saving, copying, forking and restoring each create a new revision labelled in sequence, a refused write creates nothing, and no revision is ever changed or deleted.

Conflict alert
The page that loses a save shows the head_moved message in an alert listing the new head's parameter changes, with Open and Keep my values buttons, and live updates never remove it.

Exact restore
Restoring a revision creates a new head whose values, source and digest equal the restored one, leaving every revision between them intact, and a refused restore changes no revision, ETag, room or event stream.

Build tape and stored snapshots
Every revision's tape lists one operation per parameter, repeat and geometry line of its Tine source, each with a stored digest, and the viewport replays each step from the stored solid, never a recomputed one, including at the public tape address.

Playhead by keyboard and touch
The Build tape slider moves by the published keys, ignored while an input method is composing, and by a captured drag that follows tick by tick and returns to its start tick when cancelled, while the viewport, readout, source highlight and value text follow and the camera stays put.

Fork from an operation
The owner forks from any operation at or after the body, creating a new head revision with the source truncated after it, and lands on it with the tape at that operation.

Gallery categories, sort, pages and skeletons
The gallery filters by category with computed counts, sorts by the published orders, appends stable twelve-part pages with Show more parts, and shows skeletons the exact size of cards from first paint until the first parts arrive.

Likes counted live
A signed-in person likes a part at most once, and every gallery, part page and dashboard count equals the like records and counts up live in every other open gallery and part page.

Dashboard
After a reload the dashboard lists the person's parts with their head revisions, their review rooms with progress, and their liked parts.

Publishing a part
A signed-in person publishes a part from Tine source, which is validated, stored with its title normalised, evaluated and saved as r1, and lands on the new part's page.

Part archives
Any readable revision downloads as a ZIP or TAR whose entries are the stored source, revision record and solids byte for byte, plus the published manifest.

Storage outage
With storage unreachable, health reports it, downloads, saves, copies, restores, forks and publishing answer 503 with nothing created, and each page shows its published outage state.

Grading routes
The grading routes create users, parts, revisions, rooms, comments, approvals and likes in one call, hold a part's evaluations, count a viewer's evaluations and drop every open event stream.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest on the published port and answers the health check.

Accounts
People sign up with email and password, confirm through a verification link that works once and only within its time-to-live, sign in landing on their return address or the dashboard, and sign out to the home page, with emails compared by the published folding.

Hero that measures its headline
The home hero prints its headline's rendered width in millimetres as the cable clip's span and rebuilds the clip on resize or input without moving the camera.

Responsive layout
At 375 by 812, 768 by 1024 and 1280 by 800 every screen shows its published layout using the published breakpoints for gallery, categories, rail and tape.

Reduced motion and motion timing
Motions run at the published durations and with reduced motion every glide, cross-fade, disclosure and dash animation becomes an immediate swap with the same end state.

Drawn chrome and route accent
Every page carries its route's accent on the body and the hidden drawn frame, vertex dots, crosshair and dimension leader at the published sizes.

Server boundary
The server is same-origin only, enforces body limits, never serves source or credentials, follows the one error order, and releases a request's database work as soon as its client leaves.

Workshop-at-night look
Pages read as a dark bench lit by one cyan glow behind the solid, in the two Stack Sans faces with measured tabular figures.

Real scene and real services
The viewport is a real WebGL scene and every saved, mailed, live and counted state comes from the real services named in this brief.

Conditional history writes
The revision history answers with a strong ETag naming its head, every save, restore and fork needs a matching If-Match, answering 428 without it and 412 with the current head when it no longer matches, and exactly one of several simultaneous writes from one head wins.

Draft kept through a reload
A losing save's values and message are kept in this browser under the published draft key, survive a reload with the conflict alert shown again, and are removed once saved or replaced by Open.

Evaluations stop when their request closes
Each superseded evaluation request is aborted by the page, and an evaluation whose request closes before its answer stops at once on whichever process runs it, delay included, with its record reading cancelled.

Refused numbers
A value outside the number grammar is refused in its field with the published message, dropped from a link and answered value_grammar by the API, and -0 gives the default digest.

Spoken values, view toolbar and modal dialogs
Each spinbutton exposes its value, limits and value text in the unit shown, the viewport toolbar is one Tab stop moved by arrow keys, and an open dialog leaves the rest of the page inert.

Findings listbox and severity contrast
Findings form a single-select listbox walked by arrows, Home, End and type-ahead with focus kept on the list, and every severity word, finding text and icon meets the published contrast ratios, dimmed stale findings included.

Compare address is history
Base, head, view and selected hunk live in the compare address, menu changes add history entries, view and hunk changes replace the entry, and reload, Back and Forward restore all four without reloading the page.

Resumable live events
Every live event is stored with its change and streamed with an increasing id, and a stream that reconnects with the last id it saw first receives exactly the missed events its audience may see.

Retries from the page
The page sends an Idempotency-Key with every creating action and reuses it only while the outcome is unknown, so a send retried after a lost answer shows its result once.

Number grammar
Every numeric value entering Tinework follows the number grammar, refusals and client rounding defined by house rule H1 in the House rules section.

Number rendering
Every rounded and displayed number follows house rule H2 in the House rules section: half-to-even rounding, U+2212, U+2009 and U+202F, decimals per context, and the E_TIMEOUT seconds.

Total order
Every list follows the code-point order and identifier tie-breaks of house rule H3 in the House rules section.

Storage-degraded mode
While part storage is unreachable every response and page follows house rule H4 in the House rules section: 503 with Retry-After, database-only 200, the Storage banner and aria-disabled controls.

Painted epoch
Every listed view carries data-epoch, starting at 0 and advancing by 1 per painted result, as house rule H5 in the House rules section states.

Derived markers
Every was, modified, stale, tape-disabled and approval marker is computed from its value against its baseline as house rule H6 in the House rules section states.

Layout and focus
Every route has no horizontal overflow at the listed widths and every modal surface traps, closes and returns focus as house rule H7 in the House rules section states.

Write replay
Every creating request honours Idempotency-Key, with Location, replay, in-progress and key_reused answers as house rule H8 in the House rules section states.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font, each with its licence.
Shipped packages (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and bundled fonts use only MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or SIL Open Font License 1.1.
The app stores data only in the provided PostgreSQL, MinIO and Valkey: no other database, no SQLite file, and no user data on local disk.
No external network asset is loaded at runtime: fonts are bundled files, icons are inline SVG, and no CDN script, stylesheet or font is referenced.
Server and browser code is written in TypeScript, and a lockfile is committed.
The provided service configuration and dev compose files are left unchanged.
